Subject: The Beacon: 400 lumens, 40 hours, 95 grams
Preview: A headlamp built around your trip, not your basecamp generator.
Body: You already know what a dead headlamp at 2 a.m. feels like.

The Northbay Beacon is built to make that less likely. It puts out 400 lumens — enough to read trail markers, set up a tent, or pick a careful line down a rocky descent. At 95 grams, it won't be the thing you notice on your head after hour six.

Runtime is up to 40 hours, so a long weekend with measured use doesn't require rationing your light. When it does need a charge, USB-C handles it — the same cable you're probably already carrying.

A note on limits: the Beacon is a trail and camp headlamp. It's not rated for technical caving or extended submersion. If that's your use case, you'll want to look elsewhere.

For most trips, though, it covers the hours that matter.
